memory_update.text: Primary direct exposures for value retail/private-label node: WMT, COST, TJX, BJ, DLTR.

The most important chokepoint variables appear to be purchasing scale, private-label sourcing/design capability, renewal/member economics, traffic durability, vendor leverage, and inventory access during discretionary weakness.

This pass did not include Kroger, Albertsons, Target, Ross, Burlington, Ollie's, Five Below, or private-label manufacturers/co-packers due to the five-candidate cap; they should be checked in a follow-up pass for grocery/off-price breadth and supplier exposure.

Need market-pricing and falsification layer later: compare same-store-sales acceleration, traffic quality, gross margin, shrink, inventory turns, valuation multiples, and whether consumer trade-down is already fully priced.
POST should be tracked as a large-cap US-listed private-label food manufacturing candidate due to 8th Avenue and private-label cereal/nut butter/pet-food exposure.
UNFI is a wholesale/private-brand infrastructure candidate for independent and specialty grocers, with Brands+ as the key evidence thread.
SENEA is below the preferred market-cap threshold but merits exception status because of direct private-label canned/frozen vegetable exposure to value-staple channels.
CALM maps to regulated/perishable staple capacity constraints and private-label grocery/club supply, especially under egg-price, avian-flu, and cage-free regulation shocks.
SYM is a second-order infrastructure/equipment vendor for high-volume value retailers and grocers seeking distribution automation and inventory-turn improvements.

TreeHouse Foods should be retained as a private-market benchmark for the private-label manufacturing chokepoint but removed from current US-listed candidate screens after its February 11, 2026 take-private completion.
Add WMT as a core direct mapping for value retail/private-label staples due to Walmart U.S. grocery scale, Great Value, Sam's Club, Member's Mark, and retail media/data monetization.
Add BJ as a focused warehouse-club/private-label candidate with Own Brands penetration and membership income metrics that are easier to isolate than Walmart or Costco.
Add TJX as the leading off-price chokepoint candidate where purchasing relationships and inventory turns may matter more than simple store count.
Add OLLI as a less obvious extreme-value/closeout retailer tied to excess-inventory sourcing and private-label supplementation.
Add UNFI as a second-order wholesale/private-label infrastructure candidate; thesis is weaker than direct retailers and requires margin, customer concentration, and owned-brand evidence.

Costco should be covered in a follow-up or leader pass: it is a core warehouse-club/private-label leader with Kirkland and high renewal economics, but omitted here to reserve slots for less obvious supplier/closeout mappings.

TreeHouse Foods would have been a high-quality private-label manufacturing pure play, but it completed a take-private transaction in February 2026 and should be tracked as private-market evidence rather than a current US-listed candidate.
Further pass should check DG, DLTR, BURL, ROST, KR, ACI, GO, CASY, SPTN, and grocery/private-label packaging or cold-chain suppliers for additional public-market mappings.

node: Value retail, clubs, off-price, dollar/value channels, and private-label staples
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe around the value-retail/private-label node. The highest-confidence direct exposures are scaled value retailers and membership/off-price formats where purchasing scale, inventory access, private-brand penetration, renewal economics, and traffic resilience can translate consumer trade-down into share gains. This is research mapping only, not a buy/sell recommendation. Expanded the US-listed universe for the value-retail/private-label supply-chain node toward upstream and enabling chokepoints rather than retailers themselves. The strongest public-market mappings are private-brand and value-staples manufacturers, grocery wholesale/private-brand platforms, regulated/perishable staple suppliers, and automation infrastructure vendors that help large retailers and clubs lower unit costs, improve inventory turns, and support omnichannel fulfillment. TreeHouse Foods was a historically obvious pure-play private-label candidate, but it completed a take-private transaction in February 2026 and should be tracked as a private benchmark rather than a current US-listed candidate. Expanded universe focuses on retailers and second-order suppliers that can monetize consumer trade-down through purchasing scale, membership economics, private-label penetration, closeout sourcing, and grocery distribution leverage. The strongest direct mappings are Walmart/Sam's Club, BJ's Wholesale Club, TJX, and Ollie's; UNFI is included as a less obvious wholesale/private-label infrastructure candidate. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
